What each tier means

Term
A term-tier card (referenceTier = "term") represents a single vocabulary term — a class or property IRI — without decomposing it into the domain · property · range tuple. CEDS term cards (23,237) cover CEDS classes and properties as standalone IRI anchors; CTDL term cards (1,027) mirror CTDL's own class/property vocabulary.
Property
A property-tier card (referenceTier = "property") is the classic hub tuple: domain class · property · range. This is the main mapping surface. CEDS has 2,777 of these; CTDL has many more (7,459) reflecting its wider property space after judgement.
Value
A value-tier card (referenceTier = "value") extends the tuple with a specific allowed value — domain · property · range · value. CEDS carries the largest value space (91,825), driven by its large codeset inventory (19,546 option values combinatorially addressed across many properties). CTDL has 5,510.
